slides.title: Which statement, made by a nursing student to the father of a 4-year-old child,
text: Question: Which statement, made by a nursing student to the father of a 4-year-old child, warrants correction by the nurse?
A. “Encourage your child to practice brushing his teeth after you have thoroughly cleaned them.”
B. “Fluoride supplements are needed if you do not have fluoridated water.”
C. “Your child’s ‘permanent teeth’ will begin to come in around 6 years of age.”
D. “Because the ‘baby teeth’ are not permanent, they are not important to the child.”
Correct answer: D. “Because the ‘baby teeth’ are not permanent, they are not important to the child.”
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• “Because the ‘baby teeth’ are not permanent, they are not important to the child.”
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• ““Because the ‘baby teeth’ are not permanent, they are not important to the child.”” – Primary teeth support nutrition, speech and spacing
Not correct:
• ““Encourage your child to practice brushing his teeth after you have thoroughly cleaned …” – Practice builds skills with supervision
• ““Fluoride supplements are needed if you do not have fluoridated water.”” – Supplementation may be indicated after assessing fluoride exposure
• ““Your child’s ‘permanent teeth’ will begin to come in around 6 years of age.”” – Permanent teeth generally emerge around age six
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: Which strategy is the best approach when initiating the physical examination of
text: Question: Which strategy is the best approach when initiating the physical examination of a 9-month-old male infant?
A. Have the parent hold the child on his or her lap.
B. Undress the infant and do a head-to-toe examination.
C. Ask the parent to leave because the infant will be upset.
D. Put the infant on the examination table and begin assessments at the head.
Correct answer: A. Have the parent hold the child on his or her lap.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Have the parent hold the child on his or her lap.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Have the parent hold the child on his or her lap.” – Parent provides security
Not correct:
• “Undress the infant and do a head-to-toe examination.” – May provoke distress
• “Ask the parent to leave because the infant will be upset.” – Separation increases anxiety
• “Put the infant on the examination table and begin assessments at the head.” – May be frightening before rapport
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

text: Question: Which action is appropriate when the nurse is assessing breath sounds of an 18-month-old crying child?
A. Let the child play with the stethoscope for distraction.
B. Ask the parent to quiet the child so the nurse can listen.
C. Auscultate breath sounds and chart that the child was crying.
D. Document that data are not available because of crying.
Correct answer: A. Let the child play with the stethoscope for distraction.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Let the child play with the stethoscope for distraction.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Let the child play with the stethoscope for distraction.” – Familiarization reduces fear
Not correct:
• “Ask the parent to quiet the child so the nurse can listen.” – May not reliably settle child
• “Auscultate breath sounds and chart that the child was crying.” – Crying limits accurate breath assessment
• “Document that data are not available because of crying.” – Attempt to obtain accurate data first

slides.title: The nursing instructor asks a nursing student to describe the process of quicken
text: Question: The nursing instructor asks a nursing student to describe the process of quickening. Which of the following statements, if made by the student, indicates an understanding of this term?
A. “It is irregular painless contractions that occur throughout pregnancy.”
B. “It is the soft blowing sound that can be heard when the uterus is auscultated.”
C. “It is the thinning of the lower uterine segment.”
D. “It is the fetal movement that is felt by the mother.”
Correct answer: D. “It is the fetal movement that is felt by the mother.”
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• “It is the fetal movement that is felt by the mother.”
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• ““It is the fetal movement that is felt by the mother.”” – Maternal perception of fetal movement
Not correct:
• ““It is irregular painless contractions that occur throughout pregnancy.”” – Describes Braxton Hicks
• ““It is the soft blowing sound that can be heard when the uterus is auscultated.”” – Describes uterine souffle
• ““It is the thinning of the lower uterine segment.”” – Describes effacement

slides.title: A pregnant patient has prenatal blood work. The Hg. is 9.3 and Hct. 23.1. The pa
text: Question: A pregnant patient has prenatal blood work. The Hg. is 9.3 and Hct. 23.1. The patient is diagnosed with anemia. Which of the following breakfast menus would provide the most absorbable iron?
A. Eggs with cheese, buttered toast, coffee
B. Sausage with cheese biscuit, decaffeinated tea
C. Oatmeal, brown sugar, apple, glass of milk
D. Eggs, sausage, toast, raisins, orange juice
Correct answer: D. Eggs, sausage, toast, raisins, orange juice
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Eggs, sausage, toast, raisins, orange juice
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Eggs, sausage, toast, raisins, orange juice” – Iron sources plus vitamin C
Not correct:
• “Eggs with cheese, buttered toast, coffee” – Less iron and vitamin C
• “Sausage with cheese biscuit, decaffeinated tea” – Less vitamin C to aid absorption
• “Oatmeal, brown sugar, apple, glass of milk” – Milk calcium may inhibit iron absorption
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 8 - Hematology, slide 8: “Vit. C enhances absorption of iron; antacids interfere”
• Unit 8 - Hematology, slide 8: “Dietary sources; organ meats, beans, leafy greens, raisins, molasses”

text: Question: The nurse is preparing to care for a client who is being admitted to the hospital with a possible diagnosis of ectopic pregnancy. The nurse develops a plan of care for the client and determines that which of the following is the priority nursing action?
A. Monitoring the apical pulse
B. Assessing for edema
C. Monitoring daily weight
D. Monitoring the temperature
Correct answer: A. Monitoring the apical pulse
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Monitoring the apical pulse
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)

Not correct:
• “Assessing for edema” – Not a primary hemorrhage indicator
• “Monitoring daily weight” – Less immediate measure of bleeding
• “Monitoring the temperature” – Less sensitive to acute hemorrhage

slides.title: A pregnant client reports to the health care clinic complaining of loss of appet
text: Question: A pregnant client reports to the health care clinic complaining of loss of appetite, weight loss, and fatigue. Following assessment, tuberculosis is suspected. A sputum culture is obtained, and Mycobacterium tuberculosis is identified in the sputum. The nurse provides instructions to the client regarding therapeutic management of tuberculosis. Which of the following instructions does the nurse provide to the client?
A. The need for therapeutic abortion is required.
B. Isoniazid (INH) plus rifampin (Rifadin) will be required for a total of 9 months.
C. Medication will not be started until after delivery of the fetus.
D. The newborn must receive medication therapy immediately following birth.
Correct answer: B. Isoniazid (INH) plus rifampin (Rifadin) will be required for a total of 9 months.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Isoniazid (INH) plus rifampin (Rifadin) will be required for a total of 9 months.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Isoniazid (INH) plus rifampin (Rifadin) will be required for a total of 9 months.” – Source regimen; active TB treatment is individualized
Not correct:
• “The need for therapeutic abortion is required.” – TB alone does not require abortion
• “Medication will not be started until after delivery of the fetus.” – Active TB should not be delayed
• “The newborn must receive medication therapy immediately following birth.” – Newborn management depends on exposure and evaluation
⚠ One detail differs from your PowerPoints.
• Unit 6 - Respiratory, slide 9: “Isoniazid (INH):  most potent TB drug. Bactericidal-given to prevent active TB in converters”
• Unit 6 - Respiratory, slide 9: “Long course of treatment 12-36 months”

The isoniazid-plus-rifampin answer is still the best of the four, but the quiz says 9 months while your slide says TB treatment is a long course of 12-36 months. Check the duration against your class notes.
Also appears in the weekly quiz for: Unit 5 (C).

text: Question: A patient presents to the clinic for her first prenatal appointment. She states that she has had a set of twins who were born at 34 weeks, a son who was born at 40 weeks, and she has had two miscarriages.
Correct answer: A. 5-2-1-1-2-3
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “5-2-1-1-2-3” – Five pregnancies, two births, one term and one preterm, two losses, three living
Not correct:
• “6-3-1-1-2-3” – Overcounts pregnancies and parity
• “5-3-1-2-2-3” – Overcounts parity and preterm births
• “5-2-1-2-2-3” – Twins count as one preterm birth
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 5 - OB and Newborn Care, slide 8: “Para: births after 20 weeks gestation”
• Unit 5 - OB and Newborn Care, slide 8: “Abortions: birth that occurs <20 weeks gestation”
Worked out with your slide definitions: gravida 5 (with this pregnancy), 2 births (twins count as one), term 1, preterm 1, abortions 2, living 3.

slides.title: A nurse admits a laboring woman to the triage area. A vaginal exam reveals a bre
text: Question: A nurse admits a laboring woman to the triage area. A vaginal exam reveals a breech presentation of the fetus. The nurse should take which of the following actions?
A. Prepare for a caesarean section.
B. Apply internal monitors.
C. Turn the mother to her side.
D. Place the mother in knee-chest position.
Correct answer: A. Prepare for a caesarean section.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Prepare for a caesarean section.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Prepare for a caesarean section.” – Breech presentation may require cesarean delivery; confirm circumstances
Not correct:
• “Apply internal monitors.” – Internal monitoring does not correct breech presentation
• “Turn the mother to her side.” – Side-lying does not correct breech presentation
• “Place the mother in knee-chest position.” – Knee-chest is used for cord prolapse, not routine breech

slides.title: The nurse is assigned to care for an infant with tetralogy of Fallot. The mother
text: Question: The nurse is assigned to care for an infant with tetralogy of Fallot. The mother of the infant calls the nurse to the room because the infant suddenly seems to be having difficulty breathing. The nurse enters the room and notes that the infant is experiencing a hypercyanotic episode. The initial nursing action is to:
A. Contact the respiratory therapy department.
B. Place the infant in a knee-chest position.
C. Place the infant in a prone position.
D. Call a code.
Correct answer: B. Place the infant in a knee-chest position.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Place the infant in a knee-chest position.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Place the infant in a knee-chest position.” – Increases systemic resistance and reduces right-to-left shunting
Not correct:
• “Contact the respiratory therapy department.” – Delays immediate intervention
• “Place the infant in a prone position.” – Does not reliably correct shunting
• “Call a code.” – Escalate if severe or unresponsive; position first as appropriate

slides.title: What is the best nursing action when a child with type 1 diabetes mellitus is sw
text: Question: What is the best nursing action when a child with type 1 diabetes mellitus is sweating, trembling, and pale?
A. Give the child 5 units of regular insulin subcutaneously.
B. Offer the child a glass of water.
C. Give the child a glass of orange juice.
D. Give the child glucagon subcutaneously.
Correct answer: C. Give the child a glass of orange juice.
Topic: Endocrine & Metabolic
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Give the child a glass of orange juice.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Give the child a glass of orange juice.” – Fast-acting carbohydrate if able to swallow
Not correct:
• “Give the child 5 units of regular insulin subcutaneously.” – Worsens hypoglycemia
• “Offer the child a glass of water.” – No glucose replacement
• “Give the child glucagon subcutaneously.” – Reserved for severe hypoglycemia or inability to swallow

slides.title: The mother of a child with an umbilical hernia calls the clinic and reports to t
text: Question: The mother of a child with an umbilical hernia calls the clinic and reports to the nurse that the child has been vomiting and is complaining of pain in the abdominal area. The nurse would most appropriately instruct the mother to:
A. Administer acetaminophen (Tylenol) suppositories to the child.
B. Contact the physician.
C. Apply an ice pack to the abdomen.
D. Keep the child on clear liquids.
Correct answer: B. Contact the physician.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Contact the physician.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Contact the physician.” – Pain and vomiting suggest incarceration or obstruction; urgent evaluation
Not correct:
• “Administer acetaminophen (Tylenol) suppositories to the child.” – Analgesia alone does not address possible incarceration
• “Apply an ice pack to the abdomen.” – Ice does not address possible strangulation
• “Keep the child on clear liquids.” – Diet change does not address possible obstruction

slides.title: A baby is scheduled for abdominal surgery for hypertrophic pyloric stenosis and
text: Question: A baby is scheduled for abdominal surgery for hypertrophic pyloric stenosis and has an NG tube to intermittent suction. When the family asks why the child has the tube, what response by the nurse is best?
A. “The nasogastric tube makes the baby more comfortable after surgery.”
B. “We can keep a more accurate measure of intake and output with the tube.”
C. “The tube is used to decrease postoperative diarrhea.”
D. “The nasogastric tube decompresses the abdomen and decreases vomiting.”
Correct answer: D. “The nasogastric tube decompresses the abdomen and decreases vomiting.”
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• “The nasogastric tube decompresses the abdomen and decreases vomiting.”
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• ““The nasogastric tube decompresses the abdomen and decreases vomiting.”” – Removes gastric contents and reduces distention
Not correct:
• ““The nasogastric tube makes the baby more comfortable after surgery.”” – Not primary purpose
• ““We can keep a more accurate measure of intake and output with the tube.”” – Output monitoring is secondary
• ““The tube is used to decrease postoperative diarrhea.”” – Does not treat diarrhea

slides.title: During a well-child visit, the nurse identifies that an 18-month-old infant is b
text: Question: During a well-child visit, the nurse identifies that an 18-month-old infant is bowlegged. What action by the nurse is most appropriate?
A. Document the finding in the chart.
B. Facilitate a referral to an orthopedist.
C. Perform further assessment of the musculoskeletal system.
D. Assess the infant’s diet history.
Correct answer: A. Document the finding in the chart.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Document the finding in the chart.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Document the finding in the chart.” – Physiologic bowlegs are common at 18 months
Not correct:
• “Facilitate a referral to an orthopedist.” – No referral solely for expected symmetric bowlegs
• “Perform further assessment of the musculoskeletal system.” – Further assessment if asymmetric, severe or persistent
• “Assess the infant’s diet history.” – Diet history may matter if rickets suspected, but typical bowlegs are expected
